idiom_name: factory function returning a valid object, spread overrides per test
implementation_notes: No builder class is needed: export a factory that returns a fresh valid object with every field defaulted (const aUser = (overrides = {}) => ({ name: 'Ada Lovelace', email: 'ada@example.com', age: 30, ...overrides })), and let each test spread only what it asserts. Object spread enumerates and overwrites own properties, which makes the override step impossible to mis-order and removes the positional-argument failure mode entirely; spreading into a new literal keeps the default object untouched. Deep graphs need nested factories or a dedicated library - fishery, loosely modelled on Ruby's factory_bot, merges typed overrides the same way - and an explicit chained builder is justified only when construction is conditional or a partially built object must be stored and amended over time.
pitfalls: The spread is shallow: nested objects and arrays are shared with the default, so a test that mutates user.address changes the base value for every later test; spread the nested level too.
Passing an explicit undefined (aUser({ email: undefined })) overwrites the default with undefined; omit absent keys rather than forwarding them.
A default object exported as a singleton and mutated in place is the classic cross-test leak; always return a new literal from the factory.
